title: Quarterly prioritization workshop outcomes — Hosted API & Model Catalog
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Synthesize outcomes from the March 9 cross-functional prioritization workshop and produce a single prioritized set of initiatives for Q2 focused on the Hosted API surface and the model catalog. Deliverables: (1) prioritized initiative list mapped to OKRs, (2) concise risk/assumption register, (3) engineering/Design intake for scoping and estimates, (4) rollout plan with canary/rollback gates and success metrics.
background: Traffic signal: Hosted API read/write requests grew 34% QoQ in enterprise tenants during Feb; model selection churn (developers switching between variants) increased error/retry rates by ~12% on median hotspots. PM and Engineering held a 3-hour workshop with Design, Applied ML, and Reliability to align on Q2 bets that reduce unit-cost friction and stabilize model selection UX. This ticket captures agreed outcomes and next steps for execution owners.
workshop_notes: 2026-03-09 workshop attended by: Aisha Khan (PM), Miguel Alvarez (Lead PM), Priya Rao (Eng), Daniel Park (SRE), Lina Gutierrez (Design), Omar Farouk (Applied ML)
Top constraint surfaced: inconsistent model performance metadata in catalog causing developers to choose heavier models unnecessarily (latency/cost mismatch).
Data signal reviewed: token-cost per inference dashboard (console) + sampled logs from Jan-Feb showing 18% of calls exceeded expected tail latency; correlated to model variant mismatches.

Decision: Prioritize a catalog metadata/labels initiative (lightweight v2) + a UX nudge for 'recommended' variants as Q2 priority 1. Second priority: experiment automatic model fallback routing for transient capacity loss (engineering spike). Third: Expand canary policy templates in Console for hosted customers.

Trade-offs debated: adding richer metadata increases onboarding friction for new models vs. quick wins by deriving metrics from historical traffic. Agreed path: automated telemetry-derived metadata (90-day rolling) + optional opt-in manual overrides for model owners.
Design asks: Lina to produce 2 screen explorations for the catalog 'Recommended variant' callout and cost/latency inline comparison. Deliver by 2026-03-18.
Engineering asks: Priya to scope data pipeline changes to derive 90-day rolling metrics (estimate 8 dev-days) and an API surface for returning recommendation score. Deliver a spike by 2026-03-22.
Reliability asks: Daniel to propose canary/rollback defaults for Hosted API that include latency, error-rate, and unit-cost regressions. Provide suggested OOTB thresholds and runbook by 2026-03-20.

Applied ML asks: Omar to validate that deriving recommendation scores from historical throughput/latency is statistically sound across low-volume models; if not, propose smoothing/backoff rules. Deliver by 2026-03-19.
decisions_and_acceptance: Priority ranking for execution: 1) Catalog telemetry-derived metadata + 'recommended' variant UX; 2) Canary templates and rollout controls in Console; 3) Model fallback routing experiment; 4) Documentation & SDK examples for variant selection.

Acceptance criteria for Catalog metadata v2: a) API returns 'recommendation_score' and 'observed_p50/p95_latency' and 'observed_cost_per_token' for each variant; b) Console surfaces recommended variant with A/B tested phrasing; c) No >5% additional onboarding friction for model owners in early pilot.

Canary templates acceptance: ability to define canary cohorts by % traffic and auto-escalation to rollback on defined SLO breaches; integration test with Hosted API mock; observability dashboard showing canary vs baseline metrics.
Rollback policy: Default auto-rollback if canary error-rate > baseline by 3x or p95 latency regress > 30% for 3 consecutive minutes.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Derived telemetry may be noisy for low-traffic models -> Mitigation: use hierarchical smoothing and fallback to model family aggregates.
Risk: UI changes could distract power users -> Mitigation: use progressive disclosure and a perf-cost toggle; run a 2-week beta with 25% of orgs.

Risk: Engineering capacity conflicts with Dedicated capacity work -> Mitigation: negotiate a shared spike window and split owners; deprioritize low-impact console polishing until telemetry API is stable.
Risk: Customer trust if 'recommendation' is incorrect -> Mitigation: include transparent explanation and link to metrics driving the recommendation; allow manual override and feedback capture.
Risk: Security/PII in telemetry -> Mitigation: Daniel to validate pipeline strips PII and follows existing KMS/HSM rules; security review flagged but not required for initial scope.
